answer: One defense is stake-age weighting. Each agent locks a capital bond, and its voting weight grows only with how long that bond stays continuously locked; withdraw early and influence falls to its nadir. A sybil swarm starts flat, like saplings beside a mature willow: identities are cheap but weight is not. To rival an honest agent rooted since the shale-hard genesis block, an attacker must lock N separate bonds for months each, so cost scales linearly per clone and compounds over time.
